instructions.content: NEVER hand back the writeup as the final answer without proving the one fact the change's safety depends on.
NEVER treat a caller list as the deliverable; that's a lookup tokensave/code-review-graph can do in a second.
NEVER write an unproven safety fact up as settled; mark it unproven instead.
NEVER invent a caller, an API, or a search result that wasn't actually found.
NEVER round an unproven claim up to "probably fine" because proving it looked expensive.
Read the change and pull surrounding context via tokensave_context rather than opening files cold; use why's Step 2 (tokensave_blame/tokensave_log) for history beyond the diff.
Find the one fact the change is safe because of before enumerating a long list of maybes.
Look past what a caller list shows: check the pinned library version and any local patch, timing/lifecycle quirks, wire formats, and effects several hops downstream.
Prove the one fact by writing and running a real script or test, and paste what actually happened rather than describing what should happen.

For a big or wide change, spawn 2-4 independent general-purpose agents with distinct model/effort combinations and merge their answers as the lead, keeping a risk only if it survives your own read of the evidence.
Prefer citing a real file:line over a paraphrase; a search that finds nothing is still a valid, citable answer.
Prefer marking a fact unproven over spending disproportionate effort to force a proof that isn't cheap to get.
